login.signIn: Sign in to Superset with GitHub or Google in the app window, then finish onboarding.

openProject.goal: In the row of selectors next to the prompt box of the new workspace page (above it on Paradev 2.0.11), the first is the project selector. It reads 'Select project' or 'No project' until a project is chosen. Make it read the name of the folder ${worktree} (the last part of that path), the project of that folder. Steps: press cmd+shift+o, Paradev's shortcut for 'Add Project from Folder'. It opens a macOS file dialog (with Cancel and Open buttons). If no such dialog shows after one wait of a second, click the project selector and choose 'Open from folder' in its menu instead. Never click inside that dialog, use only keys there: press cmd+shift+g, type ${worktree}, press enter, wait one second, and press enter again; the dialog then closes, a note 'Project imported and selected.' shows, and the selector reads the project name. Never type anything unless that file dialog is on the screen: without it the text goes into the composer. Never press enter in the composer, never send a message, and never choose 'Create new project' or 'Clone from URL'. If the file dialog has not opened after two tries, answer fail and say what the screen shows.

Only look, click nothing. In the row of selectors next to the prompt box, the project selector must read the name of the folder ${worktree} (the last part of that path), and the model selector below the prompt box must still read Opus 5.5 High. If both are true, answer done. If the project selector reads 'No project', 'Select project' or any other name, or the model selector reads anything else, answer fail and say what they read.

claude.goal: This step needs Paradev's new workspace page: the prompt box 'Do anything in Paradev' in the middle of the window, with 'Select project', 'Worktree' and 'This device' above it, and 'Full access' and the model selector below it. If a workspace terminal shows instead, press cmd+n and look again. The model selector is the button at the right below the prompt box; it reads 'Default model Default' until a model is chosen. Make it read 'Opus 5.5 High'. Click it; the orange asterisk (Claude) in the row of agent icons at the top of its menu must be the underlined one. Click 'Search models', type Opus 5.5, and click the row 'Opus 5.5' (not the row 'Opus'). Then click the selector again: the slider at the bottom of its menu has six stops, Default, Low, Medium, High, xHigh and Max from left to right, and the label above it names the choice. Click the fourth stop so the label reads High, then press escape. Change nothing else, and never send a message. Answer done only when the closed selector reads Opus 5.5 High.

timed.newThread cmd+n is NEW_WORKSPACE (hotkeys/registry.ts), which creates a worktree and branch under ~/.superset/worktrees (ADES 3.7). timed.send enter is an assumption for the agent TUI prompt. OPEN_SETTINGS is meta+comma (registry.ts).

Global writes at launch: Claude hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json and Codex hooks in ~/.codex/hooks.json (agent-wrappers-claude-codex-opencode.ts), skills in ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills, commands in ~/.agents/commands (managed-skills.ts). The reset must restore ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.agents.

Auto-update: auto-updater.ts sets autoDownload and autoInstallOnAppQuit to true. Checks are skipped when the DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK env var is set (macOS). A profile step cannot set an env var, so the harness must set it before open.
Telemetry is on by default (renderer DEFAULT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED is true). The stored opt-out setting was not found by name. Opt-out is a GUI item.

The skill drives the `superset`/`paradev` CLI (agents create, terminals), which lives in the bundle; the pilot must confirm it is on PATH inside the workspace terminal and that each worker is its own Claude session (orchestration.workers sessions).

BLOCKER 1 (Track A replay): the agent's environment is built by Superset (HOME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, ZDOTDIR, SUPERSET_* and a few more; ps eww, names only); launchd's ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is not passed to the agent claude, only to the haiku naming call spawned by host-service. So A4/A8/A10/A11 prompts reach the real API, not the replay server.

BLOCKER 2: every new workspace is a new folder, and Claude Code shows its 'Accessing workspace ... Yes, I trust this folder' prompt (default 'No, exit') in the terminal before it runs. ~/.superset/worktrees is not trusted in ~/.claude.json (only ~/arena is), so every timed prompt would stall on that question.
Process names: host-service.js and pty-daemon.js run as /Applications/Superset.app/Contents/MacOS/Superset (same executable name as the app), so a lookup by name alone can pick a windowless pid.

Quit: with a workspace terminal open, an AppleScript quit shows 'Are you sure you want to quit?' (Cancel / Quit, Quit is the default; settings.confirm_on_quit in ~/.superset/local.db, SQLite, so reset.jsonKeys cannot turn it off). Enter confirms. After a forced kill the next launch asks to reopen windows.

2026-11-20, blockers 1 and 2 from the bundle and the bench account. BLOCKER 1 is app-side and now routed round: buildTerminalEnv keeps only ALLOWED_ENV_VARS plus the SUPERSET_ and LC_ prefixes, so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL can never reach the workspace claude through the process environment. The adapter writes the block's replay URL into the env object of ~/.claude/settings.json instead (syncClaudeSettingsEnv in macos.ts, called from launch and send and cleared again at quit), which Claude Code applies to every session; the run loop also clears the managed keys before every block's reset, so a crashed Superset block cannot leak them into the next ADE. Codex has no such file, so its Track A replay is still open, and configure.codex is empty anyway. BLOCKER 2 cannot be fixed by account setup: Claude Code keys trust on the repo root, trust on a parent folder does not carry to child worktrees (pilot comment in macos.ts, and the bench account's .claude.json holds one entry per emdash worktree), and Superset makes a new worktree per workspace with a fresh slug. claudeTrustScanDirs therefore lists the worktrees roots and the adapter trusts every folder under them on a 250 ms timer while the app runs. Which home 2.0.8 uses is settled on the bench account: ~/.superset/app-state.json says lastRunVersion 2.0.8 with files touched 12 Nov, while ~/.paradev froze at 2.0.5 on 11 Nov, so the live home is ~/.superset (the bundle prefers ~/.paradev and falls back to the legacy dir when the move cannot run); both worktrees roots are scanned for that reason. Paradev 2.0.11 is not installed here, so its home dir is unverified.
